on_record: Ripple's Oct. 14, 2026 release says DriveWealth is integrating RLUSD, not XRP, on the XRP Ledger for collateral funding, starting in Europe with a planned U.S. expansion. That is an announced integration, not confirmed live XRP collateral settlement.

on_record: RLUSD is issued and settled on the XRPL, but reported direct settlement was about $5.08 billion by May 2026 and supply about $2.4 billion, not trillions. No record shows a trillion-dollar settlement flow in process on the ledger.

Mastercard has listed the XRPL as one of eight optional stablecoin-settlement chains and joined related pilots and events, which is not the same as this platform using the ledger.

claim: Ripple is giving institutions access to perpetual futures on more than 100 traditional markets, tapping a roughly $9 billion sector.
on_record: Ripple said on Oct. 15, 2026 that Ripple Prime launched institutional swaps referencing perpetual futures across more than 100 traditional markets. Contemporaneous reporting puts real-world-asset perpetual open interest at about $9 billion, the sector described.

on_record: Garlinghouse discussed using the XRP Ledger to earn and an institutional credit direction, but sourced remarks do not show him detailing a compliance layer that opens the network to regulated US credit markets. Those features are described as part of proposed XLS-66 lending amendments that were not activated.

name: Versan Aljarrah (Black Swan Capitalist)
text: RippleNet is the rails. XRP is the bridge asset that moves value across them. Two layers of the same system. Learn how it works and the argument disappears.
claim: RippleNet is the payment rails and XRP is the bridge asset that moves value across them, as two layers of one system.
on_record: Ripple describes RippleNet as its payment network and XRP as an optional bridge asset via On-Demand Liquidity, but most RippleNet payments settle without using XRP. Treating XRP as the asset that moves value across the rails overstates how the system actually works.

on_record: The post states a same-day market-cap comparison with Myanmar GDP. No contemporaneous market-cap print or official GDP figure in the available record confirms both numbers as of 17 October 2026.
